g1.want: tools/doororder.py finishes, and test_door_rows.py's slowest case stays under the 180s per-test timeout

i1.what: one CallGraph scope evaluation costs time proportional to the sum of the value-set sizes it touches

i2.what: metta._atoms.model.encode's return slot holds 3,104 abstract references, and every frozenset union, difference and membership over it is linear in that size

i3.what: the order must be maintained while the graph is still being discovered

i4.what: verdicts become more conservative, so the generated _orders.py changes

a1.title: schedule scopes by a topological number maintained as call edges are discovered, instead of a FIFO deque

a2.title: process the worklist depth-first, popping the newest scope

a3.title: widen a value set past a threshold to one unknown reference

a4.title: intern each Reference to an integer and carry Values as an int bitmask, so union, difference and membership stop being linear in set size

a5.title: memoise the container item-slot union in _protocol's __iter__ expansion, through the class's existing _memo that evicts when a read slot grows

a6.title: memoise the same container item-slot union in _assign's destructuring branch, keyed by the element slot it reads

a7.title: keep memoising the pure recomputations the profile names, now _container_call and what remains of _protocol

a7.1.title: name the union one concept, _stored(container, slot), and have all three sites call it

r1.says: the door-order lane and the door-rows suite both fail on the merged tree

r2.says: 13,557 evaluations take 200s on the merged tree against 20,843 in 13.8s without the classes-line modules: 0.66ms each becomes 14.8ms each

r3.says: _put instrumentation names it as the slot feeding the container with 427 readers

c1.says: chaotic iteration reaches the same least fixed point under any fair order

r4.says: standard for monotone fixed points over a finite lattice

c2.says: the configuration that does not finish performs FEWER scope evaluations than the one that finishes

r5.says: 20,843 over 2,358 scopes in 13.80s against 13,557 over 2,532 scopes in 200s

r6.says: measured: it touched fewer slots, 71,488, and still did not finish in 300s

r7.says: c2 shows the count of evaluations is not what grew, so an order that reduces that count has nothing to remove

r8.says: it changes verdicts, and this repository refuses a sound-but-incomplete default without a differential proving the gate safe

r9.says: profiled: _protocol self time 63.0s to 11.4s, Reference.__hash__ calls 515M to 158M, and 2.4x more store writes in the same 150s window

c3.says: the union of a container's two item slots is a pure store lookup, so the existing _memo's eviction on slot growth is the whole correctness condition

c4.says: the missing memo is a pre-existing inefficiency the merged tree exposed, not the thing that changed: the same code analysed the branch tip in 14.9s without it

r11.says: doororder.py measured at 14.9s on 14f5c43b5, whose _analysis.py is identical in this respect

c5.says: a5 therefore moves the threshold rather than removing the superlinearity, unless the cost after it stops growing faster than the program

r12.says: follows from c4; the completion time now being measured decides it

r13.says: profiled: _assign's 16.7s of self time and its 133M-call generator both leave the profile, and the same store work now happens in 120s where it took 150s

c6.says: after a5 and a6 the dominant cost is _put copying a frozenset on every growth, which is linear in the slot's current size

r14.says: profiled: _put is 24.8s of self time over 10.6M calls, 2.3us each, and previous | added copies the whole previous set

c7.says: an int bitmask makes union and difference 3x to 77x faster and element iteration 13x to 22x SLOWER, and this analysis iterates far more than it unions

r15.says: microbenchmark at set sizes 32, 256 and 2048 against the profile's split: about 25s of set algebra in _put and _get against 35s or more of iteration in _protocol, _container_call and set.update

r16.says: c7: the mix falls on the iteration side, so the representation change is a net loss here, unlike the points-to setting it comes from

r17.says: a5 and a6 are the same move and each was measured to work

r18.says: the same union appeared three times, in the __iter__ expansion, in destructuring and in _container_call's key selection
